title: Sentaku
description: Laundry on a line seen from underneath against a cobalt sky, the sun hidden behind a sheer polka-dot dress. Every garment was cut out of the photograph and hangs as its own sheet of cloth from its pegs, and the pointer is the wind: sweep across and a gust runs down the line from that side, the dresses billow and lift, the folds that turn to the sun catch it, the line swings under the load, and the sun shows through the dress, or past it, wherever it really is. Left alone, a summer breeze keeps them breathing.
intent: Washing on a Japanese balcony line from below, Sugimoto-quiet, crossed with iOS Spatial Scenes (https://www.macrumors.com/how-to/ios-3d-lock-screen-effect-spatial-scenes/): a real photograph broken into layers and given real physics. Each garment is a SAM 2.1 cut-out (guided-filter matte, colour unmixed against the plate, the backlit pale ring eroded off its edge and the edge lit warm from the sun instead) on a coarse XPBD cloth grid (small steps, Macklin et al. 2019, https://mmacklin.com/smallsteps.pdf) pinned where it meets the line, the photographed drape taken as the equilibrium of weight and tension (away from it, weight pulls each vertex back as on a pendulum the length of its hang, g / hang), driven by a quadratic wind pressure on each triangle, with the air a filled skirt holds acting as a pressure along its normals, one-sided links along every row so a gust can open a garment but never wring it edge-on, and down every column so a hem can never fold up over the cloth above it, and the free edge downwind fluttering; folds finer than the grid are shaded per pixel from the gradient of the drawn displacement; the line's sag plane swings as a damped pendulum toward atan(lateral load / weight). The plate behind is a smooth sky fit with LaMa grain and the sun modelled back under the dress from its visible glare. The dress is sheer: it is stored as fabric plus a share of the sky behind it, so the sun shows through it where the sun is. Lit per vertex from the cloth's normal against its rest normal (sun behind the line, sky above), graded with the shared film kit (summer). The view is pitched 56 degrees further toward the zenith than the photograph, and its eye has one constraint: at rest the sun must sit behind the dress's mid-body, as it does in the photograph. The sun is at infinity, so that puts the eye on one line, the sun-dress axis through the skirt along the sun's ray, and it slides up that axis in under the line to a hand's span in front of the skirt, just above its hem, so the sun glows through the sheer cloth in the hero view and the hem passes close below the lens. There the disc is a source of its own, since the photograph's glow would shrink to a milky patch on the magnified skirt: a hot core and a bloom about a dress-width across, through the sheer cloth and on into the sky, the fabric's own light following its forward lobe, and a thin warm ring wherever the outline passes through it. It is drawn through a stereographic lens about 115 degrees across (r = 2f tan(theta/2), conformal, so nothing stretches at the edges): the sky, at infinity, by the rotation's exact inverse map per pixel, carried on past the photograph from its smooth sky fit by angle; the cloth and the line by full perspective per vertex, each placed in 3D on the photograph's own ray to it (so from the photograph's eye it is the photograph) on a plane turned 20 degrees so the line recedes, plus the cloth's displacement. From below, gravity points at the lens: the line and its pegs recede and converge, the garments' sides converge on the zenith above the frame, and the hems come toward the lens and loom. It tilts up on a spring on load, the lens easing from the photograph's own rectilinear one to the stereographic and the eye moving in as it goes. ?gust=0..1 holds a steady gust (&dir=-1|1, &t=seconds), ?still=1 shows the photograph, ?tilt=degrees sets the pitch (0 is the photograph's own view and eye), ?fwd slides the eye along the sun-dress axis.

sources.author: Liosha Shyp (@liosha_shyp), Unsplash
sources.note: Cropped to the upper line (top 3080 of 4000 px) and worked at 1400 px wide. Garment mattes by tools/depth/segment.py prompt (SAM 2.1 Hiera-Tiny, Apache-2.0), hole filled by tools/depth/fill.py (LaMa big-lama ONNX by Carve, Apache-2.0) for grain, the clothesline fitted as a curve. Bakes: tools/depth/bakes/sentaku/.
